item.title: Windermere boathouse controversy continues
item.description: The town of Windermere heads into boathouse mediation Wednesday, Feb. 25. The Windermere Town Council has approved a resolution for a law firm to assess the viability of the appeal.

item.title: Three Birds Café supporters plan demonstration
item.description: The demonstration is planned for 10:30 a.m. Friday, Feb. 20, outside the cafe, 2 W. Plant St., Winter Garden.

item.title: Outback Steakhouse in Hamlin to open soon
item.description: The restaurant will host a grand opening at 3 p.m. Tuesday, March 3.

item.title: Orlando Health — Health Central to expand cardiology services
item.description: Advanced electrophysiology and arrhythmia care will be available in the spring.

item.title: Matthew's Hope receives matching donation
item.description: An anonymous donor has made up to $35,000 in matching money available to help replace funds the nonprofit used to operate its freeze warning emergency shelters.

item.title: Ruby and Rust to close doors by end of the month
item.description: The Winter Garden houseplant boutique has announced it will be closing its doors by the end of February.

item.title: Williams Holiday House resolves code enforcement issues
item.description: The holiday house owners announced many issues have been positively resolved.

item.title: Dead fish surface at Newton Park
item.description: Multiple tilapia fish were found dead along Lake Apopka's shoreline at Newton Park, 31 W. Garden Ave., Winter Garden, due to cold weather.

item.title: Orange County plans warming centers as cold front approaches
item.description: Orange County is closely monitoring the weather as temperatures are expected to drop below 40 degrees early next week.

item.title: Windermere Police Department gets reaccredited
item.description: Police Chief David Ogden took to social media to celebrate the department’s accomplishment.
